articles.title: SJAA Dues Increase Notice
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board announced an increase in annual membership dues to $20 ($10 for Juniors), effective August 1, 2005. This marks the first increase in ten years, driven by rising operational costs, particularly for printing the Ephemeris and a significant surge in liability insurance premiums. Despite the necessity, the club aims to continue supporting its various programs and affiliations.

articles.title: SJAA Now Accepts PayPal
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has implemented PayPal as a new, convenient option for membership renewals, streamlining the process for its members. This update allows for immediate payment transmission and renewal processing, while also offering credit card payments for those without a PayPal account, and retaining traditional mail-in forms as an alternative. A security Q&A is available for members with concerns.

articles.title: Food For Thought
articles.summary: This article discusses two lunar topics: the observation of a Transient Lunar Phenomenon (TLP) known as the "Lunar Donut," which the author observed but couldn't verify its disappearance, and the history behind the lunar crater "Baco." The author clarifies that "Baco" is an officially adopted German misspelling of Roger Bacon's name, expressing frustration with this peculiar naming convention for lunar features.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky: Planets and Stars, and a Deep Impact
articles.summary: This article details various astronomical events for July, including close passes of Mercury and Venus with the Beehive cluster and each other, the Moon's passes by the Pleiades and an occultation of Antares, and optimal viewing times for Jupiter and other planets. It also highlights the "Deep Impact" mission's impending collision with Comet Tempel 1, the return-to-flight Space Shuttle Discovery mission, and the opening of CalStar registration for an upcoming star party.

articles.title: ASP Position Announcement
articles.summary: The Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP) in San Francisco is seeking a full-time Astronomy Educator for an NSF-funded project. This role involves developing hands-on activities and toolkits, training educators at small science museums and nature centers, and assisting with distance learning programs. The position requires a Bachelor's degree in sciences with experience in informal education and outreach, preferably in astronomy.

articles.title: Solar System Stats for July 2005
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed ephemeris for various Solar System bodies for July 2005, including Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and the Sun. For specific dates (July 1, 11, 21), it lists their Right Ascension (RA), Declination (Dec.), distance from Earth in Astronomical Units (AU), apparent magnitude (Mag), and apparent angular size. The data is adapted from authoritative astronomical handbooks, serving as a reference for celestial positions and visibility.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides an updated status for its telescope loaner program, outlining which scopes are immediately available to members and how to borrow them. It also lists telescopes currently on loan with their due dates, scopes with extended loan periods, and members on a waiting list for popular instruments. Members can contact Mike Koop to arrange a loan.
